Request for help · iPod classic

iPod Classic Firmware Data

I research the Apple firmware of the iPod. I need data from a real iPod classic to test my tools. This page tells you how to collect it with one script on a Mac or a Windows PC. The script only reads the iPod. It does not copy your music, photos or videos.

Which iPods

All three iPod classic generations help. Each generation has a different firmware.

iPod classic
6th generation, 80 GB and 160 GB (2007)MB029 MB147 MB145 MB1501.1.2
6.5th generation, 120 GB (2008)MB562 MB5652.0.1
7th generation, thin 160 GB (2009)MC293 MC2972.0.4

The highlighted row is the generation that helps most now: the research already examined its firmware file. The last column is the last Apple firmware for each generation. To see the model and the version of your iPod, go to Settings > About on the iPod. An older version also helps.

What the script collects

It copies

  • The firmware partition: the hidden first part of the iPod disk.
  • The partition table: the first block of the disk.
  • The device files in iPod_Control/Device. They give the model and the serial number.
  • The disk and USB information from macOS or Windows.
  • The names of the folders in iPod_Control, without the names of the music files.

It does not copy

  • Music, audiobooks, podcasts and videos.
  • Photos and album artwork.
  • Contacts, calendars and notes.
  • Your music library database. You can add it if you want (refer to the steps).
  • Any file outside the iPod.

The ZIP file contains a list of each file and its SHA-256 checksum (MANIFEST.txt). You can open the ZIP file and examine it before you send it.

Privacy

CAUTION

The ZIP file contains the serial number of your iPod. The firmware partition can also contain a sleep image of the iPod memory, with recent items from the screen. Send the file only to the person who sent you this page.

CAUTION

The ZIP file contains Apple firmware. Do not post it in a public place, for example a forum or a public GitHub repository.

Before you start

  • A Mac with macOS 12 or later, or a PC with Windows 10 or 11. The script does not operate on Linux.
  • The USB cable of the iPod.
  • Approximately 500 MB of free space on the computer.
  • The password of an administrator account of the computer.
  • Approximately 10 minutes.
Steps on a MacSteps on Windows

Steps on a Mac

  1. Give Terminal Full Disk Access

    Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access. Turn on Terminal. If Terminal is not in the list, click + and select Applications > Utilities > Terminal.

    macOS does not let a program read a disk directly without this permission. Turn it off again after step 9.

  2. Connect the iPod

    Connect the iPod to the Mac with the USB cable. Wait until the iPod shows in Finder. Do not connect another iPod at the same time.

  3. Copy the script

    The button copies the script to the clipboard. You can read the script in The scripts below.

  4. Save the script on the Desktop

    Open Terminal (Applications > Utilities). Paste this command and push Return:

    pbpaste > ~/Desktop/collect-ipod-info.sh

    This command writes the clipboard to a file. It shows no output.

  5. Start the script

    bash ~/Desktop/collect-ipod-info.sh

  6. Enter your password

    Terminal asks for the password of your Mac account. The characters do not show while you type. Push Return.

    The script needs administrator rights only to read the hidden firmware partition.

  7. Wait

    The script reads the firmware partition. This takes some minutes. Do not disconnect the iPod. At the end, the script shows Done. Nothing was written to the iPod. and the name of the ZIP file on your Desktop.

    Optional: to also send the music library database (song names, without music), start the script with --library at the end of the command in step 5. This helps the research, but it shows your music collection.

  8. Eject the iPod

    In Finder, click the eject button next to the iPod. Then disconnect it.

  9. Send the ZIP file

    Send the file ipod-info-….zip from your Desktop to the person who sent you this page. Use a private link, for example from iCloud Drive or Dropbox. The file is approximately 100 MB or larger. In the message, give the model and the version from Settings > About.

    Then turn off Full Disk Access for Terminal, and delete collect-ipod-info.sh from your Desktop.

Steps on Windows

  1. Connect the iPod

    Connect the iPod to the PC with the USB cable. Wait until File Explorer shows it. If iTunes opens, do not sync the iPod. Do not connect another iPod at the same time.

  2. Copy the script

  3. Open PowerShell as administrator

    Click Start and type PowerShell. Click "Run as administrator". When Windows asks for permission, click Yes.

    The script needs administrator rights only to read the hidden firmware partition.

  4. Go to the Desktop

    Paste this command into PowerShell and push Enter:

    cd ([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop'))

    To paste in PowerShell, right-click in the window.

  5. Save the script on the Desktop

    Click "Copy Windows Script" in step 2 again. Then paste this command and push Enter:

    Get-Clipboard -Raw | Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 collect-ipod-info.ps1

    Step 4 replaced the script on the clipboard with a command. Thus you must copy the script again. This command shows no output.

  6. Start the script

    Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Force; .\collect-ipod-info.ps1

    The first part lets this window run the script. It applies only to this window. It does not change a setting of Windows.

  7. Wait

    The script reads the firmware partition. This takes some minutes. Do not disconnect the iPod. At the end, the script shows Done. Nothing was written to the iPod. and the name of the ZIP file on your Desktop.

    Optional: to also send the music library database (song names, without music), add -Library at the end of the command in step 6. This helps the research, but it shows your music collection.

  8. Eject the iPod

    In File Explorer, right-click the iPod and click Eject. Then disconnect it.

  9. Send the ZIP file

    Send the file ipod-info-….zip from your Desktop to the person who sent you this page. Use a private link, for example from OneDrive or Dropbox. The file is approximately 100 MB or larger. In the message, give the model and the version from Settings > About.

    Then delete collect-ipod-info.ps1 from your Desktop.

If the script stops

The script stops at the first problem and writes nothing. Do the step for the message that you see. This script is new and it is not tested on every iPod. If you see a different message, send the text of the message.

MessageWhat to do
No iPod found.Connect the iPod. Wait until Finder shows it. Start the script again.
More than one iPod foundDisconnect the other iPods.
Cannot read /dev/rdisk…Mac: do step 1 again. Quit Terminal completely and open it again. Then start the script again.
Do not start the script with sudo.Mac: start the script without sudo, as in step 5. The script asks for the password itself.
The temporary folder of the system … is not usable.Mac: close Terminal, open it again and start the script again. Windows: the TEMP setting points to a drive root such as C:\. Send the text of the message.
Start PowerShell as administratorWindows: close PowerShell. Do step 3 again, and click "Run as administrator".
Cannot read the diskWindows: close iTunes. Make sure that PowerShell runs as administrator. Start the script again.
…cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled…Windows: use the full command in step 6. Its first part allows the script in this window.
The partition table is not MBR or APM.Send the file block0.bin from the folder that the message names.
Short readUse a different USB port or cable. Do not touch the iPod while the script reads it.
WARNING: The firmware partition does not start with the Apple STOP banner.This is not an error. The script continues. Send the ZIP file: it shows what the iPod has.
The iPod volume is not mounted.This is not an error. The script continues, but it cannot copy the device files. If Finder or File Explorer does not show the iPod, send the ZIP file anyway.

The scripts

The Mac script uses only programs that macOS includes: diskutil, ioreg, dd and ditto. The Windows script uses only Windows PowerShell. It opens the disk with read access only. Both scripts write only to a new temporary folder and to the ZIP file on your Desktop. They collect the same files. At the end, they remove only the files that they wrote, one at a time. They never delete a folder with its contents, and they never follow a link.

Show the Mac script (collect-ipod-info.sh, version 3) 
#!/bin/bash
# collect-ipod-info.sh: collects the firmware data of a connected iPod into one ZIP file, for research.
#
# The script only reads the iPod. It never writes to it. It does not copy music, photos, videos,
# contacts, calendars or notes. Without --library, it does not copy the music library database.
#
# It collects:
#   - the firmware partition (the first partition of the iPod disk), as a .bin file;
#   - the first block of the disk (the partition table);
#   - the device information files in iPod_Control/Device (for example SysInfoExtended);
#   - the disk and USB information from macOS (diskutil and ioreg);
#   - with --library: the files in iPod_Control/iTunes (the library database, without music files).
#
# Usage:
#   bash collect-ipod-info.sh [--disk diskN] [--library] [--no-firmware]
#
# The read of the raw disk needs administrator rights: the script uses sudo and asks for your password.
# Terminal must have Full Disk Access (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access).
#
# Test mode (no iPod, no sudo): IPOD_TEST_IMAGE=disk.img IPOD_TEST_BLOCK=512 [IPOD_TEST_VOLUME=dir] bash collect-ipod-info.sh
set -euo pipefail

VERSION=3
MAX_PARTITION=$((512 * 1024 * 1024))      # a firmware partition is smaller; a larger value is an error
DISK=""
LIBRARY=0
FIRMWARE=1

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --disk) DISK="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --library) LIBRARY=1; shift ;;
        --no-firmware) FIRMWARE=0; shift ;;
        -h|--help) sed -n '2,22p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
        *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done

fail() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

# -- find the iPod ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

TEST_IMAGE="${IPOD_TEST_IMAGE:-}"
if [ -n "$TEST_IMAGE" ]; then
    [ -f "$TEST_IMAGE" ] || fail "IPOD_TEST_IMAGE is not a file."
    DISK="test"
    RAW="$TEST_IMAGE"
    BS="${IPOD_TEST_BLOCK:-512}"
    VOLUME="${IPOD_TEST_VOLUME:-}"
    SUDO=()
else
    [ "$(uname)" = "Darwin" ] || fail "This script is for macOS."
    media_name() { diskutil info "$1" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *Device \/ Media Name: *//p'; }
    if [ -z "$DISK" ]; then
        FOUND=()
        for d in $(diskutil list external physical 2>/dev/null | awk '/^\/dev\/disk/ {sub("/dev/", "", $1); print $1}'); do
            case "$(media_name "$d" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in *ipod*) FOUND+=("$d") ;; esac
        done
        [ ${#FOUND[@]} -eq 0 ] && fail "No iPod found. Connect the iPod and make sure that Finder shows it."
        [ ${#FOUND[@]} -gt 1 ] && fail "More than one iPod found (${FOUND[*]}). Connect only one, or use --disk diskN."
        DISK="${FOUND[0]}"
    fi
    case "$(media_name "$DISK" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in
        *ipod*) ;;
        *) fail "$DISK is not an iPod (media name: \"$(media_name "$DISK")\")." ;;
    esac
    RAW="/dev/r$DISK"
    BS="$(diskutil info "$DISK" | sed -n 's/^ *Device Block Size: *\([0-9]*\) Bytes.*/\1/p')"
    [ -n "$BS" ] || fail "Cannot read the block size of $DISK."
    VOLUME=""
    for s in $(diskutil list "$DISK" | awk '{print $NF}' | grep "^${DISK}s"); do
        m="$(diskutil info "$s" | sed -n 's/^ *Mount Point: *//p')"
        if [ -n "$m" ] && [ -d "$m/iPod_Control" ]; then VOLUME="$m"; break; fi
    done
    SUDO=(sudo)
fi

STAMP="$(date +%Y-%m-%d_%H.%M.%S)"
# Hard limits for the temporary folder. The script removes its files at the end, so:
#  - the script must not run as root (it uses sudo only for the reads of the raw disk);
#  - the temporary folder of the system must be an absolute path, not "/", and must exist;
#  - mktemp makes a new folder with a random name; the name must have the exact pattern.
# At the end, the script never deletes recursively. Refer to remove_temp_files below.
[ "$(id -u)" != 0 ] || fail "Do not start the script with sudo. The script asks for your password when it needs it."
TMPBASE="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
TMPBASE="${TMPBASE%/}"
case "$TMPBASE" in
    /?*) ;;
    *) fail "The temporary folder of the system (TMPDIR=\"${TMPDIR:-}\") is not usable." ;;
esac
[ -d "$TMPBASE" ] || fail "The temporary folder of the system (\"$TMPBASE\") does not exist."
WORK="$(mktemp -d "$TMPBASE/ipod-info.XXXXXXXX")" || fail "Cannot make a temporary folder."
case "$WORK" in
    "$TMPBASE"/ipod-info.????????) ;;
    *) fail "Unexpected temporary folder: \"$WORK\"." ;;
esac
[ -d "$WORK" ] && [ "$WORK" != "/" ] || fail "Unexpected temporary folder: \"$WORK\"."
OUT="$WORK/ipod-info-$STAMP"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
echo "==> iPod: $DISK (block size $BS bytes). The files go to a temporary folder first."

# Reads COUNT blocks of BLOCK bytes at block SKIP of the raw disk to standard output. Read only.
read_raw() { ${SUDO[@]+"${SUDO[@]}"} dd if="$RAW" bs="$1" skip="$2" count="$3" 2>/dev/null; }

hex_at() { od -An -tx1 -j"$2" -N"$3" "$1" | tr -d ' \n'; }          # FILE OFFSET COUNT -> hex
le32() { local h; h="$(hex_at "$1" "$2" 4)"; echo $((16#${h:6:2}${h:4:2}${h:2:2}${h:0:2})); }
be32() { local h; h="$(hex_at "$1" "$2" 4)"; echo $((16#$h)); }

# -- information from macOS ------------------------------------------------------------------------

{
    echo "collect-ipod-info.sh version $VERSION"
    echo "date: $STAMP"
    echo "macOS: $(sw_vers -productVersion 2>/dev/null || uname -r)"
    echo "disk: $DISK"
    echo "block size: $BS"
    echo "volume: ${VOLUME:-not mounted}"
    echo "options: library=$LIBRARY firmware=$FIRMWARE"
} > "$OUT/info.txt"
if [ -z "$TEST_IMAGE" ]; then
    diskutil info "$DISK" > "$OUT/diskutil-info.txt" 2>&1 || true
    diskutil list "$DISK" > "$OUT/diskutil-list.txt" 2>&1 || true
    ioreg -p IOUSB -w0 -l -r -n iPod > "$OUT/ioreg-usb.txt" 2>&1 || true
fi

# -- the partition table and the firmware partition ------------------------------------------------

if [ "$FIRMWARE" = 1 ]; then
    echo "==> Reading the partition table (your password can be necessary)."
    read_raw "$BS" 0 1 > "$OUT/block0.bin" || fail "Cannot read $RAW. Give Terminal Full Disk Access, then try again."
    [ -s "$OUT/block0.bin" ] || fail "Cannot read $RAW. Give Terminal Full Disk Access, then try again."
    LBA=""; COUNT_SECTORS=""
    if [ "$(hex_at "$OUT/block0.bin" 510 2)" = "55aa" ]; then
        TYPE0=$((16#$(hex_at "$OUT/block0.bin" 450 1)))
        LBA=$(le32 "$OUT/block0.bin" 454)
        COUNT_SECTORS=$(le32 "$OUT/block0.bin" 458)
        echo "partition table: MBR (Windows format), entry 0 type $TYPE0, start sector $LBA, sectors $COUNT_SECTORS" >> "$OUT/info.txt"
        [ "$TYPE0" = 0 ] || fail "The first partition is not an iPod firmware partition (type $TYPE0)."
    elif [ "$(hex_at "$OUT/block0.bin" 0 2)" = "4552" ]; then                     # "ER": Apple partition map
        MUL=$(( 16#$(hex_at "$OUT/block0.bin" 2 1) / 2 ))
        COUNT=1; BLK=1
        while [ "$BLK" -le "$COUNT" ] && [ "$BLK" -lt 64 ]; do
            OFF=$(( BLK * MUL * 512 ))
            read_raw "$BS" $(( OFF / BS )) 1 > "$OUT/apm-entry.bin"
            E=$(( OFF % BS ))
            [ "$(hex_at "$OUT/apm-entry.bin" "$E" 2)" = "504d" ] || break                 # "PM"
            COUNT=$(be32 "$OUT/apm-entry.bin" $(( E + 4 )))
            if [ "$(hex_at "$OUT/apm-entry.bin" $(( E + 48 )) 10)" = "4170706c655f4d444657" ]; then   # "Apple_MDFW"
                LBA=$(be32 "$OUT/apm-entry.bin" $(( E + 8 )))
                COUNT_SECTORS=$(be32 "$OUT/apm-entry.bin" $(( E + 12 )))
                break
            fi
            BLK=$(( BLK + 1 ))
        done
        rm -f "$OUT/apm-entry.bin"
        echo "partition table: APM (Mac format), Apple_MDFW start sector ${LBA:-none}, sectors ${COUNT_SECTORS:-none}" >> "$OUT/info.txt"
    else
        fail "The partition table is not MBR or APM. Send the file $OUT/block0.bin instead."
    fi
    [ -n "$LBA" ] && [ -n "$COUNT_SECTORS" ] || fail "No firmware partition found."

    # The partition table gives sectors. iPodFirm uses the block size that the system reports as the
    # sector size. Some iPods report a block size that is not the unit of their partition table. Thus
    # try the reported block size first, then 512, 2048 and 4096 bytes. Use the first unit where the
    # partition starts with the Apple STOP banner "{{~~".
    banner_at() {                                   # OFFSET -> success if "{{~~" is at OFFSET
        local first=$(( $1 / BS )) pre=$(( $1 % BS )) n=1
        [ $(( pre + 4 )) -gt "$BS" ] && n=2
        read_raw "$BS" "$first" "$n" > "$OUT/probe.bin" || return 1
        [ "$(hex_at "$OUT/probe.bin" "$pre" 4)" = "7b7b7e7e" ]
    }
    UNIT=""; TRIED=""
    for u in "$BS" 512 2048 4096; do
        case " $TRIED " in *" $u "*) continue ;; esac
        TRIED="$TRIED $u"
        [ $(( COUNT_SECTORS * u )) -le "$MAX_PARTITION" ] || continue
        if banner_at $(( LBA * u )); then UNIT=$u; break; fi
    done
    rm -f "$OUT/probe.bin"
    if [ -n "$UNIT" ]; then
        echo "sector unit: $UNIT bytes (the STOP banner is at the start of the partition)" >> "$OUT/info.txt"
    else
        UNIT=$BS
        echo "sector unit: $BS bytes (no STOP banner found with the units$TRIED)" >> "$OUT/info.txt"
        echo "    WARNING: The firmware partition does not start with the Apple STOP banner. The script continues."
    fi
    START=$(( LBA * UNIT ))
    SIZE=$(( COUNT_SECTORS * UNIT ))
    [ "$SIZE" -gt 0 ] && [ "$SIZE" -le "$MAX_PARTITION" ] || fail "The firmware partition size ($SIZE bytes) is not plausible."

    echo "==> Reading the firmware partition ($((SIZE / 1048576)) MB). This takes some minutes."
    if [ $(( START % BS )) -eq 0 ] && [ $(( SIZE % BS )) -eq 0 ]; then
        CHUNK=$BS
        for k in 2048 256 32; do
            if [ $(( START % (BS * k) )) -eq 0 ] && [ $(( SIZE % (BS * k) )) -eq 0 ]; then CHUNK=$(( BS * k )); break; fi
        done
        read_raw "$CHUNK" $(( START / CHUNK )) $(( SIZE / CHUNK )) > "$OUT/firmware-partition.bin"
    else
        # The partition does not start or end on a block boundary: read whole blocks, then cut.
        PRE=$(( START % BS ))
        read_raw "$BS" $(( START / BS )) $(( (PRE + SIZE + BS - 1) / BS )) > "$OUT/blocks.bin"
        tail -c +$(( PRE + 1 )) "$OUT/blocks.bin" | head -c "$SIZE" > "$OUT/firmware-partition.bin"
        rm -f "$OUT/blocks.bin"
    fi
    GOT=$(wc -c < "$OUT/firmware-partition.bin" | tr -d ' ')
    [ "$GOT" -eq "$SIZE" ] || fail "Short read: $GOT of $SIZE bytes."

    # A short check of the result. The full analysis is done later.
    F="$OUT/firmware-partition.bin"
    {
        echo "firmware partition bytes: $GOT"
        echo "STOP banner: $([ "$(head -c 4 "$F")" = "{{~~" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
        echo "]ih[ magic: $([ "$(hex_at "$F" 256 4)" = "5d69685b" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
        D=$(le32 "$F" 260)
        echo "directory value at 0x104: $D"
        echo "directory at value + 0x200: $(hex_at "$F" $(( D + 512 )) 8)"
        echo "directory at value + 0x1000: $(hex_at "$F" $(( D + 4096 )) 8)"
    } >> "$OUT/info.txt"
fi

# -- files on the iPod volume ---------------------------------------------------------------------

if [ -n "$VOLUME" ] && [ -d "$VOLUME/iPod_Control" ]; then
    echo "==> Copying the device information files."
    if [ -d "$VOLUME/iPod_Control/Device" ]; then
        mkdir -p "$OUT/iPod_Control/Device"
        find "$VOLUME/iPod_Control/Device" -maxdepth 1 -type f -size -2048k ! -name '._*' -exec cp {} "$OUT/iPod_Control/Device/" \;
    fi
    # The names of the folders in iPod_Control, without the names of the music files.
    find "$VOLUME/iPod_Control" -maxdepth 2 -type d ! -path "*/Music/*" | sed "s#^$VOLUME/##" | LC_ALL=C sort > "$OUT/ipod-control-folders.txt"
    if [ "$LIBRARY" = 1 ] && [ -d "$VOLUME/iPod_Control/iTunes" ]; then
        echo "==> Copying the library database (no music files)."
        mkdir -p "$OUT/iPod_Control"
        # Only regular files: find -type f does not follow a link and does not list one.
        (cd "$VOLUME/iPod_Control" && find iTunes -type f ! -name '._*' -print0) |
            while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
                mkdir -p "$OUT/iPod_Control/$(dirname "$f")"
                cp -p "$VOLUME/iPod_Control/$f" "$OUT/iPod_Control/$f"
            done
    fi
else
    echo "volume files: not copied (the iPod volume is not mounted)" >> "$OUT/info.txt"
    echo "    The iPod volume is not mounted. The device information files are not copied."
fi

# -- the ZIP file -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

(cd "$OUT" && find . -type f ! -name MANIFEST.txt -print0 | sort -z | xargs -0 shasum -a 256 > MANIFEST.txt)
DEST="${IPOD_OUT_DIR:-$HOME/Desktop}"
ZIP="$DEST/ipod-info-$STAMP.zip"
N=2
while [ -e "$ZIP" ]; do ZIP="$DEST/ipod-info-$STAMP-$N.zip"; N=$((N + 1)); done
ditto -c -k --keepParent "$OUT" "$ZIP"

# Removes the temporary files without a recursive delete:
#  1. each file in MANIFEST.txt (the script made the list), one at a time, only if it is a regular
#     file (not a link) and its real folder is inside the real temporary folder;
#  2. each folder, deepest first, with rmdir, which removes only an empty folder.
# Anything else stays, and the script shows where it is.
remove_temp_files() {
    local out_real line rel f dir_real
    out_real="$(cd "$OUT" && pwd -P)" || return 1
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        rel="${line#*  ./}"
        case "$rel" in ""|/*|*..*) continue ;; esac
        f="$OUT/$rel"
        [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
        dir_real="$(cd "$(dirname "$f")" && pwd -P)" || continue
        case "$dir_real" in "$out_real"|"$out_real"/*) rm -f -- "$f" ;; esac
    done < "$OUT/MANIFEST.txt"
    rm -f -- "$OUT/MANIFEST.txt"
    find "$OUT" -depth -type d -exec rmdir {} \; 2>/dev/null
    rmdir "$WORK" 2>/dev/null
}
remove_temp_files || true
[ -d "$WORK" ] && echo "    Some temporary files were not removed. They are in: $WORK"
echo
echo "==> Done. Nothing was written to the iPod."
echo "    File:   $ZIP"
echo "    Size:   $(du -h "$ZIP" | cut -f1)"
echo "    SHA-256: $(shasum -a 256 "$ZIP" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
if [ "$FIRMWARE" = 1 ]; then
    echo "    Send this file privately. It contains Apple firmware. Do not post it in public."
else
    echo "    Send this file privately."
fi
Show the Windows script (collect-ipod-info.ps1, version 3) 
# collect-ipod-info.ps1: collects the firmware data of a connected iPod into one ZIP file, for research.
# The Windows version of collect-ipod-info.sh. It collects the same files.
#
# The script only reads the iPod. It never writes to it. It opens the disk with read access only.
# It does not copy music, photos, videos, contacts, calendars or notes. Without -Library, it does
# not copy the music library database.
#
# It collects:
#   - the firmware partition (the first partition of the iPod disk), as a .bin file;
#   - the first block of the disk (the partition table);
#   - the device information files in iPod_Control\Device (for example SysInfoExtended);
#   - the disk and USB information from Windows (Get-Disk, Get-PnpDevice);
#   - with -Library: the files in iPod_Control\iTunes (the library database, without music files).
#
# Usage (in PowerShell, started as administrator):
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\collect-ipod-info.ps1 [-Disk N] [-Library] [-NoFirmware]
#
# It needs Windows 10 or 11 (Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7).
#
# Test mode (no iPod, no administrator rights; also on macOS with pwsh):
#   $env:IPOD_TEST_IMAGE = 'disk.img'; $env:IPOD_TEST_BLOCK = '512'; $env:IPOD_TEST_VOLUME = 'folder'
param(
    [int]$Disk = -1,
    [switch]$Library,
    [switch]$NoFirmware
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$Version = 3
$MaxPartition = [long]512 * 1024 * 1024        # a firmware partition is smaller; a larger value is an error

function Fail([string]$Message) {
    Write-Host "ERROR: $Message" -ForegroundColor Red
    exit 1
}

# -- find the iPod ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

$TestImage = $env:IPOD_TEST_IMAGE
$Volume = $null
if ($TestImage) {
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $TestImage -PathType Leaf)) { Fail 'IPOD_TEST_IMAGE is not a file.' }
    $DiskName = 'test'
    $Raw = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $TestImage).Path
    $BS = [long]512
    if ($env:IPOD_TEST_BLOCK) { $BS = [long]$env:IPOD_TEST_BLOCK }
    if ($env:IPOD_TEST_VOLUME) { $Volume = $env:IPOD_TEST_VOLUME }
} else {
    $principal = New-Object Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal([Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent())
    if (-not $principal.IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)) {
        Fail 'Start PowerShell as administrator: right-click PowerShell, then select "Run as administrator".'
    }
    $isIPod = { param($d) ("$($d.FriendlyName) $($d.Model)") -match 'ipod' }
    if ($Disk -ge 0) {
        $d = Get-Disk -Number $Disk
        if (-not (& $isIPod $d)) { Fail "Disk $Disk is not an iPod (name: `"$($d.FriendlyName)`")." }
    } else {
        $found = @(Get-Disk | Where-Object { & $isIPod $_ })
        if ($found.Count -eq 0) { Fail 'No iPod found. Connect the iPod and wait until Windows shows it.' }
        if ($found.Count -gt 1) { Fail ("More than one iPod found (disks " + (($found | ForEach-Object { $_.Number }) -join ', ') + '). Connect only one, or use -Disk N.') }
        $d = $found[0]
    }
    $DiskName = "PhysicalDrive$($d.Number)"
    $Raw = "\\.\PhysicalDrive$($d.Number)"
    $BS = [long]$d.LogicalSectorSize
    if ($BS -le 0) { Fail "Cannot read the block size of disk $($d.Number)." }
    foreach ($p in @(Get-Partition -DiskNumber $d.Number -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
        if ($p.DriveLetter -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath "$($p.DriveLetter):\iPod_Control")) { $Volume = "$($p.DriveLetter):\"; break }
    }
    # Windows PowerShell 5.1 (.NET Framework) does not open "\\.\" paths with a FileStream.
    # CreateFile with GENERIC_READ gives a handle that can only read.
    Add-Type -TypeDefinition @'
using System;
using System.IO;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
using Microsoft.Win32.SafeHandles;
public static class IPodRawDisk {
    [DllImport("kernel32.dll", SetLastError = true, CharSet = CharSet.Unicode)]
    static extern SafeFileHandle CreateFile(string name, uint access, uint share, IntPtr security,
                                            uint disposition, uint flags, IntPtr template);
    public static FileStream OpenRead(string path) {
        // 0x80000000 = GENERIC_READ; 3 = FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE; 3 = OPEN_EXISTING
        SafeFileHandle h = CreateFile(path, 0x80000000, 3, IntPtr.Zero, 3, 0, IntPtr.Zero);
        if (h.IsInvalid) { throw new System.ComponentModel.Win32Exception(Marshal.GetLastWin32Error()); }
        return new FileStream(h, FileAccess.Read, 1);
    }
}
'@
}

function Open-Raw {
    if ($TestImage) { return [System.IO.File]::Open($Raw, 'Open', 'Read', 'ReadWrite') }
    return [IPodRawDisk]::OpenRead($Raw)
}

# Copies LENGTH bytes at OFFSET of the raw disk to a file. Read only. OFFSET and LENGTH are multiples of the block size.
function Read-Raw([long]$Offset, [long]$Length, [string]$OutFile) {
    $in = Open-Raw
    try {
        $out = [System.IO.File]::Create($OutFile)
        try {
            [void]$in.Seek($Offset, 'Begin')
            $chunk = [long]1048576
            if ($chunk % $BS -ne 0) { $chunk = $BS }
            $buffer = New-Object byte[] $chunk
            $left = $Length
            while ($left -gt 0) {
                $n = [int][Math]::Min($chunk, $left)
                $got = $in.Read($buffer, 0, $n)
                if ($got -le 0) { break }
                $out.Write($buffer, 0, $got)
                $left -= $got
            }
        } finally { $out.Close() }
    } finally { $in.Close() }
}

function Get-LE32([byte[]]$B, [int]$At) { return [long][BitConverter]::ToUInt32($B, $At) }
function Get-BE32([byte[]]$B, [int]$At) { return ([long]$B[$At] -shl 24) + ([long]$B[$At + 1] -shl 16) + ([long]$B[$At + 2] -shl 8) + [long]$B[$At + 3] }
function Get-Hex([byte[]]$B, [int]$At, [int]$Count) { return (($B[$At..($At + $Count - 1)] | ForEach-Object { $_.ToString('x2') }) -join '') }

# Hard limits for the temporary folder. The script removes its files at the end, so:
#  - the temporary folder of the system must not be a drive root (for example C:\) or empty;
#  - the script makes a new folder with a random name; the folder must not exist before;
#  - at the end, the script never deletes recursively and never goes into a junction or a link.
#    Refer to Remove-TempFiles below.
$Stamp = Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd_HH.mm.ss'
$tempBase = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()).TrimEnd('\', '/')
if (-not $tempBase -or $tempBase -match '^[A-Za-z]:$' -or $tempBase -match '^\\\\[^\\]+\\[^\\]+$' -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $tempBase -PathType Container)) {
    Fail "The temporary folder of the system (`"$([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath())`") is not usable. Set TEMP and TMP to a folder that is not a drive root."
}
$Temp = Join-Path $tempBase ("ipod-info-" + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Temp) { Fail "The temporary folder $Temp exists already." }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Temp | Out-Null
$Out = Join-Path $Temp "ipod-info-$Stamp"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Out | Out-Null

# Lists the files (or the folders, deepest first) under a folder. It does not go into a junction or
# a symbolic link, and it does not list one. Windows PowerShell 5.1 can follow a junction in a
# recursive Get-ChildItem or Remove-Item.
function Get-OwnFiles([string]$Dir) {
    foreach ($item in @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $Dir -Force)) {
        if ($item.Attributes -band [System.IO.FileAttributes]::ReparsePoint) { continue }
        if ($item.PSIsContainer) { Get-OwnFiles $item.FullName } else { $item }
    }
}
function Get-OwnFolders([string]$Dir) {
    foreach ($item in @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $Dir -Force -Directory)) {
        if ($item.Attributes -band [System.IO.FileAttributes]::ReparsePoint) { continue }
        Get-OwnFolders $item.FullName
        $item.FullName
    }
}
Write-Host "==> iPod: $DiskName (block size $BS bytes). The files go to a temporary folder first."
$Info = Join-Path $Out 'info.txt'
function Add-Info([string]$Line) { Add-Content -LiteralPath $Info -Value $Line -Encoding UTF8 }

# -- information from Windows ----------------------------------------------------------------------

Add-Info "collect-ipod-info.ps1 version $Version"
Add-Info "date: $Stamp"
Add-Info "windows: $([Environment]::OSVersion.VersionString), PowerShell $($PSVersionTable.PSVersion)"
Add-Info "disk: $DiskName"
Add-Info "block size: $BS"
if ($Volume) { Add-Info "volume: $Volume" } else { Add-Info 'volume: not mounted' }
Add-Info "options: library=$([int][bool]$Library) firmware=$([int](-not $NoFirmware))"
if (-not $TestImage) {
    $d | Format-List * | Out-File -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Out 'disk-info.txt') -Encoding UTF8
    Get-Partition -DiskNumber $d.Number -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Format-List * | Out-File -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Out 'partitions.txt') -Encoding UTF8
    Get-PnpDevice -PresentOnly -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.FriendlyName -match 'ipod' -or $_.InstanceId -match 'VID_05AC' } |
        Format-List FriendlyName, Class, Status, InstanceId | Out-File -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Out 'usb-devices.txt') -Encoding UTF8
}

# -- the partition table and the firmware partition ------------------------------------------------

if (-not $NoFirmware) {
    Write-Host '==> Reading the partition table.'
    $block0File = Join-Path $Out 'block0.bin'
    try { Read-Raw 0 $BS $block0File } catch { Fail "Cannot read the disk ($($_.Exception.Message)). Start PowerShell as administrator, then try again." }
    $b0 = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($block0File)
    if ($b0.Length -lt 512) { Fail 'Cannot read the first block of the disk.' }
    $lba = $null; $sectors = $null
    if ($b0[510] -eq 0x55 -and $b0[511] -eq 0xAA) {
        $type0 = [int]$b0[450]
        $lba = Get-LE32 $b0 454
        $sectors = Get-LE32 $b0 458
        Add-Info "partition table: MBR (Windows format), entry 0 type $type0, start sector $lba, sectors $sectors"
        if ($type0 -ne 0) { Fail "The first partition is not an iPod firmware partition (type $type0)." }
    } elseif ($b0[0] -eq 0x45 -and $b0[1] -eq 0x52) {                       # "ER": Apple partition map
        $mul = [long][Math]::Floor($b0[2] / 2)
        $count = 1; $blk = 1
        $entryFile = Join-Path $Out 'apm-entry.bin'
        while ($blk -le $count -and $blk -lt 64) {
            $off = $blk * $mul * 512
            Read-Raw ([long]([Math]::Floor($off / $BS)) * $BS) $BS $entryFile
            $e = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($entryFile)
            $at = [int]($off % $BS)
            if (-not ($e[$at] -eq 0x50 -and $e[$at + 1] -eq 0x4D)) { break }               # "PM"
            $count = Get-BE32 $e ($at + 4)
            if ((Get-Hex $e ($at + 48) 10) -eq '4170706c655f4d444657') {                   # "Apple_MDFW"
                $lba = Get-BE32 $e ($at + 8)
                $sectors = Get-BE32 $e ($at + 12)
                break
            }
            $blk++
        }
        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $entryFile -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        Add-Info "partition table: APM (Mac format), Apple_MDFW start sector $lba, sectors $sectors"
    } else {
        Fail "The partition table is not MBR or APM. Send the file $block0File instead."
    }
    if ($null -eq $lba -or $null -eq $sectors) { Fail 'No firmware partition found.' }

    # The partition table gives sectors. iPodFirm uses the block size that the system reports as the
    # sector size. Some iPods report a block size that is not the unit of their partition table. Thus
    # try the reported block size first, then 512, 2048 and 4096 bytes. Use the first unit where the
    # partition starts with the Apple STOP banner "{{~~".
    $probe = Join-Path $Out 'probe.bin'
    $unit = $null; $tried = @()
    foreach ($u in @($BS, 512, 2048, 4096)) {
        if ($tried -contains [long]$u) { continue }
        $tried += [long]$u
        if ($sectors * $u -gt $MaxPartition) { continue }
        $offset = $lba * $u
        $pre = $offset % $BS
        $blocks = if ($pre + 4 -gt $BS) { 2 } else { 1 }
        try { Read-Raw ($offset - $pre) ($blocks * $BS) $probe } catch { continue }
        $p = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($probe)
        if ($p.Length -ge $pre + 4 -and (Get-Hex $p ([int]$pre) 4) -eq '7b7b7e7e') { $unit = [long]$u; break }
    }
    Remove-Item -LiteralPath $probe -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($unit) {
        Add-Info "sector unit: $unit bytes (the STOP banner is at the start of the partition)"
    } else {
        $unit = $BS
        Add-Info "sector unit: $BS bytes (no STOP banner found with the units $($tried -join ' '))"
        Write-Host '    WARNING: The firmware partition does not start with the Apple STOP banner. The script continues.'
    }
    $start = $lba * $unit
    $size = $sectors * $unit
    if ($size -le 0 -or $size -gt $MaxPartition) { Fail "The firmware partition size ($size bytes) is not plausible." }

    Write-Host "==> Reading the firmware partition ($([Math]::Floor($size / 1MB)) MB). This takes some minutes."
    $fw = Join-Path $Out 'firmware-partition.bin'
    if ($start % $BS -eq 0 -and $size % $BS -eq 0) {
        Read-Raw $start $size $fw
    } else {
        # The partition does not start or end on a block boundary: read whole blocks, then cut.
        $pre = $start % $BS
        $blocksFile = Join-Path $Out 'blocks.bin'
        Read-Raw ($start - $pre) ([long][Math]::Ceiling(($pre + $size) / $BS) * $BS) $blocksFile
        $in = [System.IO.File]::OpenRead($blocksFile)
        try {
            $outStream = [System.IO.File]::Create($fw)
            try {
                [void]$in.Seek($pre, 'Begin')
                $buffer = New-Object byte[] 1048576
                $left = $size
                while ($left -gt 0) {
                    $got = $in.Read($buffer, 0, [int][Math]::Min($buffer.Length, $left))
                    if ($got -le 0) { break }
                    $outStream.Write($buffer, 0, $got)
                    $left -= $got
                }
            } finally { $outStream.Close() }
        } finally { $in.Close() }
        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $blocksFile -Force
    }
    $got = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $fw).Length
    if ($got -ne $size) { Fail "Short read: $got of $size bytes." }

    # A short check of the result. The full analysis is done later.
    $head = New-Object byte[] 0x2000
    $fs = [System.IO.File]::OpenRead($fw)
    try { [void]$fs.Read($head, 0, $head.Length) } finally { $fs.Close() }
    Add-Info "firmware partition bytes: $got"
    Add-Info ("STOP banner: " + $(if ((Get-Hex $head 0 4) -eq '7b7b7e7e') { 'yes' } else { 'no' }))
    Add-Info ("]ih[ magic: " + $(if ((Get-Hex $head 256 4) -eq '5d69685b') { 'yes' } else { 'no' }))
    $dirValue = Get-LE32 $head 260
    Add-Info "directory value at 0x104: $dirValue"
    $full = $null
    foreach ($delta in 512, 4096) {
        $pos = $dirValue + $delta
        if ($pos + 8 -le $head.Length) { $hex = Get-Hex $head ([int]$pos) 8 }
        else {
            if ($null -eq $full) { $full = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($fw) }
            $hex = if ($pos + 8 -le $full.Length) { Get-Hex $full ([int]$pos) 8 } else { 'outside' }
        }
        $label = if ($delta -eq 512) { '0x200' } else { '0x1000' }
        Add-Info "directory at value + ${label}: $hex"
    }
}

# -- files on the iPod volume ---------------------------------------------------------------------

$control = if ($Volume) { Join-Path $Volume 'iPod_Control' } else { $null }
if ($control -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $control)) {
    Write-Host '==> Copying the device information files.'
    $device = Join-Path $control 'Device'
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $device) {
        $dest = Join-Path (Join-Path $Out 'iPod_Control') 'Device'
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dest -Force | Out-Null
        Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $device -File -Force | Where-Object { $_.Length -lt 2MB -and -not $_.Name.StartsWith('._') } |
            ForEach-Object { Copy-Item -LiteralPath $_.FullName -Destination $dest -Force }
    }
    # The names of the folders in iPod_Control, without the names of the music files.
    $names = @('iPod_Control')
    foreach ($dir in Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $control -Directory -Force) {
        $names += "iPod_Control/$($dir.Name)"
        if ($dir.Name -ne 'Music') {
            foreach ($sub in Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $dir.FullName -Directory -Force) { $names += "iPod_Control/$($dir.Name)/$($sub.Name)" }
        }
    }
    $sorted = [string[]]$names
    [Array]::Sort($sorted, [StringComparer]::Ordinal)       # the same sequence as LC_ALL=C sort in the macOS script
    $sorted | Out-File -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Out 'ipod-control-folders.txt') -Encoding UTF8
    $itunes = Join-Path $control 'iTunes'
    if ($Library -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $itunes)) {
        Write-Host '==> Copying the library database (no music files).'
        $dest = Join-Path $Out 'iPod_Control'
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dest -Force | Out-Null
        # Only regular files: Get-OwnFiles does not go into a junction or a link. Copy-Item -Recurse can.
        $itunesFull = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $itunes -Force).FullName.TrimEnd('\', '/')
        foreach ($f in @(Get-OwnFiles $itunesFull)) {
            if ($f.Name.StartsWith('._')) { continue }
            $target = Join-Path (Join-Path $dest 'iTunes') $f.FullName.Substring($itunesFull.Length + 1)
            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path (Split-Path -Parent $target) -Force | Out-Null
            Copy-Item -LiteralPath $f.FullName -Destination $target -Force
        }
    }
} else {
    Add-Info 'volume files: not copied (the iPod volume is not mounted)'
    Write-Host '    The iPod volume is not mounted. The device information files are not copied.'
}

# -- the ZIP file -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# MANIFEST.txt has the format of "shasum -a 256", so "shasum -c MANIFEST.txt" can verify it.
$lines = foreach ($f in @(Get-OwnFiles $Out) | Sort-Object FullName) {
    $rel = './' + $f.FullName.Substring($Out.Length + 1).Replace('\', '/')
    "$((Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $f.FullName -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower())  $rel"
}
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllLines((Join-Path $Out 'MANIFEST.txt'), [string[]]$lines)

$dest = $env:IPOD_OUT_DIR
if (-not $dest) { $dest = [Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop') }
$zip = Join-Path $dest "ipod-info-$Stamp.zip"
$n = 2
while (Test-Path -LiteralPath $zip) { $zip = Join-Path $dest "ipod-info-$Stamp-$n.zip"; $n++ }
# The entry names use "/". Compress-Archive in PowerShell 5.1 writes "\", and a Mac then shows wrong names.
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression.FileSystem
$top = Split-Path -Leaf $Out
$archive = [System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::Open($zip, [System.IO.Compression.ZipArchiveMode]::Create)
try {
    foreach ($f in @(Get-OwnFiles $Out) | Sort-Object FullName) {
        $entry = "$top/" + $f.FullName.Substring($Out.Length + 1).Replace('\', '/')
        [void][System.IO.Compression.ZipFileExtensions]::CreateEntryFromFile($archive, $f.FullName, $entry, [System.IO.Compression.CompressionLevel]::Optimal)
    }
} finally { $archive.Dispose() }
# Removes the temporary files without a recursive delete:
#  1. each file that Get-OwnFiles lists (no junctions, no links), one at a time, only if its full
#     path is inside the temporary folder of this script;
#  2. each folder, deepest first, with Directory.Delete(path, $false), which removes only an empty folder.
# Anything else stays, and the script shows where it is.
function Remove-TempFiles {
    $root = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($Temp).TrimEnd('\', '/')
    $sep = [System.IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar
    foreach ($f in @(Get-OwnFiles $root)) {
        $full = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($f.FullName)
        if ($full.StartsWith($root + $sep, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {
            Remove-Item -LiteralPath $full -Force
        }
    }
    foreach ($d in @(Get-OwnFolders $root) + $root) {
        try { [System.IO.Directory]::Delete($d, $false) } catch { }
    }
}
try { Remove-TempFiles } catch { }
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Temp) { Write-Host "    Some temporary files were not removed. They are in: $Temp" }

Write-Host ''
Write-Host '==> Done. Nothing was written to the iPod.'
Write-Host "    File:    $zip"
Write-Host ("    Size:    {0:N1} MB" -f ((Get-Item -LiteralPath $zip).Length / 1MB))
Write-Host "    SHA-256: $((Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $zip -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower())"
if (-not $NoFirmware) {
    Write-Host '    Send this file privately. It contains Apple firmware. Do not post it in public.'
} else {
    Write-Host '    Send this file privately.'
}
Thank you. Your data helps to test tools for the iPod classic firmware, so that they identify each model correctly.
